text_blocks.snippet: Cushing's syndrome and Addison's disease are both conditions related to the adrenal glands, but they have opposite effects on cortisol levels. Cushing's syndrome involves excessive cortisol production, while Addison's disease involves insufficient cortisol production. Both can cause fatigue, weight changes, and other similar symptoms, but the specific patterns and additional symptoms differ.
snippet_highlighted_words: both conditions related to the adrenal glands, but they have opposite effects on cortisol levels

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: Often caused by long-term use of corticosteroids (medications) or by tumors in the pituitary or adrenal glands that lead to overproduction of cortisol.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Can include weight gain, particularly in the upper body, a rounded face, high blood sugar, high blood pressure, and thin bones.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Focuses on addressing the underlying cause, which may involve surgery to remove tumors or adjusting medication dosages.

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: Primarily caused by autoimmune destruction of the adrenal glands, but can also be due to other factors like infections or tumors.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Can include fatigue, muscle weakness, weight loss, low blood pressure, and skin hyperpigmentation (darkening of the skin).

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Involves lifelong hormone replacement therapy with corticosteroids to compensate for the lack of natural cortisol production.

list.title: Cortisol Levels:
list.snippet: Cushing's syndrome involves excess cortisol, while Addison's disease involves a deficiency.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Cushing's syndrome can manifest with distinct physical changes like a rounded face and stretch marks, while Addison's disease symptoms can be more subtle and felt internally.

list.title: Treatment Approaches:
list.snippet: Cushing's syndrome treatment often involves addressing the root cause (e.g., tumor removal), while Addison's disease treatment primarily focuses on hormone replacement therapy.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, Cushing's syndrome is a condition of cortisol excess, while Addison's disease is a condition of cortisol deficiency, requiring different approaches to management and treatment.
